text: Jobs growth came in at barely half of forecasts (57K vs 115K expected) while the Fed is now considering rate hikes instead of cuts due to sticky inflation at 3.5% — this combination of slowing hiring and tightening bias raises the risk of a policy mistake that hurts stocks, so consider holding extra cash.
RGTI is your worst position at -53% with revenue shrinking, heavy cash burn, and extreme short interest — the thesis is broken and holding further risks more damage to your portfolio.
QBTS is down 39% with no profits, negative free cash flow, and 20% short interest meaning professional traders are betting against it — exit now before losses deepen.
IONQ is down 56% from its highs, unprofitable, burning cash with high short interest and insiders selling — there's no fundamental reason to keep holding this position.

SILG.L has bearish technicals across the board and sits 37% below its high — reduce your silver exposure since commodity positions with this kind of technical damage tend to take a long time to recover.

META is down 30% from its high but has 22% revenue growth and a PE under 15 which is genuinely cheap for a company this profitable — this pullback looks like an opportunity to add shares at a discount.
Adobe has a PE of just 9 with solid 10% revenue and free cash flow growth plus insider buying — that valuation is unusually cheap for a high-quality software company and worth adding to.

Eli Lilly's 45% revenue growth is best-in-class, insiders are buying with their own money, and the earnings beat streak shows the business is consistently outperforming expectations — worth adding on any dip.
